title: Australia's Energy Balance: Consumption, Supply and the Petroleum Challenge
summary: A whole-of-economy view of Australian energy connecting the electricity mix with state pathways, industry demand and petroleum exposure.
key_takeaway: Cleaner electricity is the foundation of Australia's transition, not its completion. State pathways, industrial energy use and petroleum dependence show that a successful power-sector policy does not automatically become an economy-wide one. The transition becomes real only when cleaner generation starts changing the fuels used in transport, industry and everything else that doesn't yet run on the grid.

inline_figures.caption: States cluster into sharply different transition pathways when renewable share and coal change are considered together.
